rules.title: Cartwright Act amendments (Assembly Bill 325) on common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Businesses may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement to restrain trade. They also may not use or offer a common pricing algorithm while coercing users to adopt its price or commercial-term recommendations. A common pricing algorithm is one with two or more users that uses competitor data.
rules.key_value: Common pricing algorithm = two or more users and use of competitor data; criminal fines up to $6 million for businesses and $1 million for individuals; civil fines up to $1 million
rules.penalty: Criminal fines of the greater of up to $6 million (corporations) or $1 million (individuals), or twice the gain or loss; civil fines of up to $1 million in actions by the Attorney General or a district attorney; treble damages, injunctive relief and attorneys' fees in private suits.
rules.status_basis: Article states Governor Newsom signed AB 325 in October 2025 and that it took effect on January 1, 2026.

coverage.summary: Applies to any business using or distributing common pricing algorithms, including apartment rental companies, with no building-based test.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Single-firm algorithms using only a business's own data are not covered.

rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
